## English

### [1.40.3] - 2026-07-27

#### Fixed

- **Reduced C / C++ header-detection allocations for large repositories** —
  Bounded lexical samples for ambiguous `.h` files are now scanned by newline
  index instead of materializing an array and a string for every sampled line.
- **Removed split-array growth from delimiter-only extractor paths** —
  Repository metadata, application manifests, VHDL declarations and package
  imports, and CUDA kernel parameters now share an allocation-free span walker
  while preserving trimming and empty-entry behavior.
- **Removed per-match closure allocations from functional-language references** —
  Erlang, OCAML, and Raku now use shared indexed span-membership checks when
  suppressing remote, qualified, quoted-atom, and type-reference matches.
- **Removed padded-line copies from functional-language state machines** —
  Erlang specification/callable terminators and Raku heredoc terminators now
  compare trimmed spans, avoiding a new string for every padded sentinel line.
- **Removed per-identifier closure allocations from hardware-language scopes** —
  Verilog, SystemVerilog, and VHDL shadow checks plus CUDA, GLSL, HLSL, Metal,
  and WGSL binding/resource checks now use direct indexed membership loops.
- **Stopped allocating empty exclusion lists on functional-language lines** —
  Erlang, OCAML, and Raku now create quoted, remote, type, qualified, and method
  span lists only after the first relevant match on a line.
- **Reduced reference-extraction allocations for large embedded multiline payloads** —
  Structurally masked C# raw strings, Java text blocks, and JavaScript /
  TypeScript template literals no longer materialize trimmed reference
  contexts for lines that will be skipped.
- **Reduced repository-metadata and manifest validation overhead** —
  Long metadata candidates now use allocation-free span character scans, while
  application manifests track dependency ancestry by XML depth instead of
  rescanning an ancestor stack for every identity.
- **Avoided duplicate full-line whitespace scans during reference extraction** —
  Every supported language now classifies each prepared line once and reuses
  the result across special-line and ordinary empty-line dispatch, which is
  especially important for long structurally masked payloads.
- **Reduced all-language extraction allocations for large source files** —
  Symbol and reference extraction now share an exact-capacity line splitter
  that avoids the temporary separator-index arrays created by generic splitting.
- **Made bounded regex enumeration demand-driven** — Extractors that stop after
  reaching a result limit no longer force every remaining regex match on the
  source line to be materialized first, while right-to-left instances preserve
  their default reverse match order. Secondary reference scanners now use the
  same streaming path across Fortran, Visual Basic, F#, Pascal, Objective-C,
  Haskell, Elixir, Smalltalk, Lua, Dart, Razor, JSON, JavaScript, GitHub Actions,
  and C++ compound requirements without changing their configured timeouts.
  Bounded reference scans now stop before requesting another match and skip
  all later extraction phases on the same dense line once capacity is reached.
  Symbol and dependency extractors now stream their remaining multi-match
  patterns across scientific/native, Pascal/Ada, SQL, Python, Swift, GraphQL,
  markup/XAML, shell, Ruby, Perl, Elixir, CSS, HDL, C++, and manifest parsing.
  Count-only scans no longer retain a `MatchCollection`, while preserving the
  previous all-or-nothing result if matching times out.
  Dense XAML supplemental symbol scans now stop as soon as the shared
  structured-data symbol budget needs its diagnostic marker, instead of
  building an unbounded temporary list and trimming it after all phases.
  Symbol container assignment now reuses one path buffer across members instead
  of allocating a stack snapshot and a second list for every nested symbol.
  Prolog goal scans now allocate per-line call lists only when a known goal is
  emitted and update directive metadata in place instead of copying the list.
  JSON symbol and reference extraction now build UTF-8 line-offset arrays at
  exact capacity instead of retaining a growing list alongside its final copy.
- **Streamed core reference matches** — Shared calls, C# attributes, types,
  patterns and locals, JSX elements, JVM documentation links, and Solidity
  scanners now consume single-pass match groups on demand.
- **Streamed dynamic-language reference matches** — PHP, Ruby, R, and Perl
  scanners now enumerate dense attribute, type, DSL, namespace/member/resource,
  and arrow-call matches only while the reference budget has capacity.
- **Streamed functional-language reference matches** — Clojure, Elixir,
  Erlang, OCAML, and Raku now enumerate regex results on demand and stop dense
  lines as soon as the per-file reference budget is full.
- **Streamed infrastructure and markup reference matches** — CSS, XAML,
  HTML/GraphQL/Markdown, HDL, MSBuild, Dockerfile, shell, and PowerShell
  scanners now consume dense match groups on demand.
- **Streamed JVM-family reference matches** — Java, Kotlin, Scala, and
  Gradle/Groovy scanners now consume dense regex results on demand and stop
  bounded reference loops once the per-file cap is reached.
- **Streamed Python reference matches** — Python decorators, annotations,
  runtime type checks, typing factories, dataclass/framework integrations, and
  dynamic imports now stop producing regex matches at the reference cap;
  decorator arguments also stream directly from their start offset.
- **Streamed SQL reference matches** — SQL statement, source, target,
  generated-column, window-clause, procedure-call, and temporary-object
  scanners now consume matches on demand and stop at bounded reference limits.
- **Streamed systems-language reference matches** — C/C++, Rust, Swift, Go,
  and shared scientific/native scanners now consume dense construction, type,
  concurrency, wrapper, and call matches on demand.
- **Removed padded suffix copies across declaration scanners** — CSS selector
  continuations, C# and Java body-less declarations, and functional-language
  sentinels now share allocation-free trimmed span comparisons.

### [1.40.2] - 2026-07-26

#### Fixed

- **MCP file-resource controls are now discoverable in-band** — `initialize` instructions now explain exact-path templates and filtered `resources/list` usage, while each list response publishes accepted parameters, bounds, and cursor semantics under `_meta.discovery_contract`, so AI clients can use current resource discovery without guessing non-standard protocol extensions.

#### Documentation

- **Downstream MCP setup no longer duplicates a cdidx command catalog** — removed the stale Code Search Rules templates and now direct AI clients to the live MCP `initialize`, `tools/list`, and resource-discovery contracts, while correcting cloud-bootstrap references to the current documentation entry points.

### [1.40.1] - 2026-07-25

#### Fixed

- **Release validation no longer flakes when macOS runners are heavily loaded** — LSP cancellation coverage now awaits an asynchronous signal without blocking thread-pool progress, and post-extraction hook timeout coverage keeps a wider separation between the callback budget and the delayed worker completion.

### [1.40.0] - 2026-07-25

#### Added

- **Doctor environment inventories are now filterable and byte-bounded, and license output is available as structured JSON (#4713)** — `doctor --env-inventory=full` accepts domain, category, and sensitivity filters plus a whole-document `--max-json-bytes` limit, while `license --json` exposes stable versioned license, commercial-use, trademark, and controlling-document fields.
- **Portable archive and database delta workflows now support bounded scopes and richer previews (#4714)** — archive export can retain selected languages, paths, projects, and non-test files, import dry-run compares the validated snapshot with an existing destination, and detailed database diff pages reference-edge and chunk drift.
- **Audit recipes can now emit bounded SARIF findings (#4715)** — `search --recipe <name> --format sarif` preserves `recipe/query` rule identity, source locations, severity and confidence, conservative truncation metadata, and stable result fingerprints while respecting per-query and total result limits; unsupported row selectors are rejected instead of being silently ignored.
- **Hook installs can now be previewed and report idempotent outcomes (#4716)** — `cdidx hooks install --dry-run` shows the planned create, managed replacement, custom-hook chain, or no-op action together with the managed hook without changing files. Real installs now distinguish `installed`, `updated`, and `already_installed`; exact executable UTF-8/no-BOM reruns leave the existing hook untouched, while unusable mode or encoding drift is repaired.
- **Suggestions now support audited manual lifecycle transitions and bounded atomic file exports (#4719)** — maintainers can explicitly move records among validated local/upstream states with redacted actor, reason, timestamp, and revision metadata; local dispositions remain distinct from upstream submissions, while Markdown and issue-draft exports safely publish up to 16 MiB through alias-protected no-overwrite or explicit atomic-replacement paths.
- **Ctags exports now explain skipped symbols and support generated-code opt-in (#4720)** — `cdidx export ctags --json` reports bounded `skip_reason_counts` plus generated-code policy metadata, excludes generated files by default, accepts `--include-generated`, and degrades safely for legacy databases without generated-file metadata.
- **Large LSP symbol responses now support bounded progress and cancellation (#4721)** — `workspace/symbol` and `textDocument/documentSymbol` honor partial-result and work-done tokens, stream deterministic chunks under item and byte limits, report truncation and accurate cancelled counts, preserve document-sync notifications and required rejection responses under queue pressure, and return the standard cancellation error when `$/cancelRequest` stops an active request.
- **MCP file resources support direct templates and bounded discovery filters (#4722)** — `resources/templates/list` now advertises `cdidx://file-path/{path}` for safe, percent-encoded resolution of a known repository-relative path while returning the canonical file-resource identity. `resources/list` adds bounded `path`, normalized `lang`, and opt-in `includeGenerated` filters, and its cursors reject filter changes between pages.
- **CLI batch now supports structured input, configurable budgets, and bounded parallel reads (#4723)** — `cdidx batch` accepts validated `{"command":"...","args":[...]}` records alongside string arrays, lets generated pipelines tune input-line and JSON-summary output budgets within safe maxima, and can run up to 16 isolated read-only workers with stable input-order records, per-item error isolation, and incremental output before stdin EOF.
- **MCP discovery and status responses now offer bounded low-context views (#4724)** — `tools/list` accepts opt-in `format: "compact"` catalogs and exact `names` filters for retrieving full definitions on demand, while the default and explicit `format: "full"` responses remain compatible. The `status` tool now accepts bounded top-level `fields` projection after full or compact formatting, so clients can request only freshness or readiness data without carrying the complete status payload.
- **Repository-wide literal find now uses an indexed candidate path (#4725)** — `find --all` uses a synchronized trigram index for safe ASCII literals before re-verifying candidate lines, while regex, normalized exact, short, non-ASCII, legacy, unsynchronized, and actively rebuilding index queries report an explicit bounded-scan fallback; `optimize --dry-run` includes both FTS indexes in its storage preview.
- **CUDA and shader languages now expose bounded reference graphs (#4737)** — CUDA, GLSL, HLSL, Metal, and WGSL now index statically visible calls, CUDA kernel launches, user-defined type uses, resources, bindings, and supported includes, with per-language metadata suppression and explicit conservative readiness semantics.
- **Scientific and native-extension languages now expose reference graphs (#4738)** — Nim, MATLAB, Julia, D, Cython, and Ada emit bounded language-aware call, import/module, and type/base references. Ambiguous `.m` files preserve content-based classification, expose a conservative MATLAB/Objective-C symbol and reference union when evidence remains unresolved, and resolve those references against definitively classified MATLAB or Objective-C files.
- **Repository metadata formats now provide structured symbol, reference, and graph capabilities (#4740)** — TOML, JSON Lines/NDJSON, Git and Docker ignore files, Git attributes, EditorConfig, and `.rules` files expose conservative sections, keys, rules, and repository-local path edges. Windows application manifests now expose dependent assembly and local file/path references, with unsafe path forms suppressed. Bounded extraction remains persistable for large inputs, including multiline TOML path arrays, compact `.rules` calls, quoted Git attributes patterns, EditorConfig character classes, and TOML-escaped Windows paths.
- **Reference graphs now cover Verilog, SystemVerilog, and VHDL (#4742)** — HDL indexing emits bounded, syntax-visible hierarchy, package/import/use, architecture/entity, and scope-aware known same-file signal/type edges for `references` and applicable graph queries. Existing indexes are automatically refreshed by the next full scan before graph readiness is restored; scoped updates and graph queries remain explicitly degraded while that refresh is pending.
- **Crystal, Groovy, Tcl, Prolog, and ambiguous `.pl` files now support conservative reference graphs (#4746)** — indexing records imports and language-appropriate calls at their source locations, recognizes command-style calls only for callables declared in the same file, parses Groovy control-statement bodies, Tcl command substitutions, inline proc declarations, variadic `after` / `namespace eval` script arguments, `dict for` bodies after bare dictionary words, and `switch` branch bodies, resolves Tcl namespace-qualified proc calls to the matching namespace, requires complete Tcl command words and excludes syntax markers, excludes Groovy closure parameter headers, limits Prolog calls to declared predicates in goal positions including top-level and same-line directives, scans Prolog clause terminators and precomputes multiline predicate-head parenthesis matches in one pass each, masks Perl quote-like regular-expression and heredoc bodies (including whitespace before quote-like delimiters and indented heredocs) in ambiguous `.pl` files without consuming fat-arrow pairs, short Prolog predicate heads, or Perl `$#array` tokens, stops extraction after Perl `__DATA__` / `__END__` markers, preserves Tcl proc and Prolog predicate caller containers, and reports structured symbol/reference/graph capabilities after `.pl` content classification. Pre-graph extractor stamps keep graph readiness degraded until a normal index refresh rewrites affected rows, and human-readable status output identifies that refresh instead of cap-hit remediation.

#### Fixed

- **Database restore and retention workflows now provide safe previews (#4717)** — database restore dry-runs validate bounded checkpoint manifests, regular-file paths, and staging space; checkpoint deletion, checkpoint retention pruning, and restore-backup pruning can preview exact deleted and retained paths without filesystem mutation.
- **Report JSON keeps a safe artifact handle when paths are redacted (#4718)** — `report --json` now returns the generated bundle basename in `output_path`, including with `--redact-paths`, while diagnostic database and parent-directory paths remain redacted.
- **Workspace member selection and status now expose unambiguous health signals (#4726)** — `workspace use` accepts normalized manifest-relative paths so repeated directory names can be selected safely, while `workspace status` reports bounded per-member database, schema, freshness, completeness, and graph-readiness details.
- **`analyze_symbol` now infers graph language from consistent reference evidence when definitions are missing (#4727)** — definition-free results expose graph-language source, confidence, candidates, and conflict metadata, infer support only when reference/caller/callee evidence agrees on one language, and leave mixed-language evidence unresolved.
- **Markdown fence-language markers no longer pollute default unused audits (#4728)** — `unused --lang markdown` now classifies fenced-code markers such as `bash`, `md`, and `python` as documentation syntax and suppresses them by default, while `--all` still returns them for raw auditing.
- **C# nested interpolated templates preserve enclosing symbols (#4729)** — The lexical masker now restores every parent interpolation frame after nested regular, verbatim, or raw strings, so raw SQL and completion templates no longer truncate enclosing class ranges. Calls inside expression-bodied properties and string contents are no longer emitted as phantom declarations, and the C# extraction contract refreshes existing indexes.
- **High-volume discovery output is resumable (#4730)** — compact search/symbol/file output, the opt-in search array envelope, and bounded language inventory now report authoritative total/omitted/truncated/stable-at metadata with opaque query- and generation-bound cursors; partial `find --all` scans return a cursor that resumes after the last scanned line.
- **Dependency-cycle audits now stay stable across display limits (#4731)** — `deps --cycles` separates its deterministic SCC graph budget from result pagination, reports whether analysis is complete, ranks cycles stably, and provides opaque continuation cursors in CLI JSON and MCP responses.
- **Full Fish completion flag parity is now regression-guarded (#4732)** — generated Fish output is checked against the canonical CLI schema and the other shells for every long flag and command scope, including `--issue-state` and `--suppress-noise`.
- **Aggregate and nested CLI help now matches accepted command behavior (#4733)** — every cataloged nested verb resolves to specific usage, constraints, side effects, and examples; index help documents non-interactive `--rebuild --yes`, aggregate dependency help includes symbol/noise filters, and suggestion export help explains formats, duplicate preflight, output writes, and read-only GitHub access.
- **Outline and unused cursors are bound to their result snapshot (#4734)** — newly emitted opaque cursors now bind the offset to normalized scope, filters, ordering, and index generation, and stale or mismatched reuse returns explicit restart-required guidance.
- **Grouped search reports complete query totals (#4735)** — bounded grouped output now distinguishes query-wide matched/group/file totals from grouped, emitted, and omitted rows, and reports truncation plus continuation guidance whenever output limits hide matches.
- **LSP document symbols keep positional record properties under their record (#4736)** — hierarchy construction now resolves indexed container, range, and same-line source-position relationships after materializing every symbol, so same-range positional and body members no longer leak to an enclosing root or a later same-named container because of presentation order.
- **CLI and configuration initialization dependencies are now acyclic (#4741)** — immutable command metadata is shared through a dependency-neutral contract, while config-source provenance is resolved separately from environment access. Source-level architecture tests prevent help/completion and workspace/config dependencies from reconnecting the cycles.
- **Clojure, Erlang, OCaml, and Raku now provide reference graphs (#4743)** — bounded, comment- and string-aware extraction records imports, aliases, calls, and type/protocol/behaviour relationships, attributes calls to their enclosing functions, and advertises reference and graph readiness for all four languages.
- **Missing definitions now return structured JSON errors (#4744)** — default-format `definition --json` lookups emit the versioned `E018_QUERY_NOT_FOUND` error and exit `2` when no symbol matches, with or without `--body`, instead of succeeding with empty stdout. Bounded envelopes preserve the error in `metadata.error` with no result rows, and the response is preflighted against `--max-json-bytes`, so an impossible cap fails without emitting oversized JSON.
- **C# nullable-generic `out` methods remain visible after nested interpolation (#4745)** — Methods such as `TryReadAllPositionLines(string, out IReadOnlyList<string?>)` now stay available to definition and outline queries after nested interpolated-string lexical context. Their declarations are not emitted as calls, and their resolved caller/callee edges remain queryable.
- **`excerpt` now accepts line-only focus (#4747)** — CLI `--focus-line` and MCP `focusLine` no longer require a focus column. When the column is omitted, long-line clamping keeps the leading window; explicit focus lengths still require a column.
- Fixed `symbols --quiet` so trailing quiet aliases suppress informational stderr without replacing text, NDJSON, or JSON-array result stdout with an empty result.
- **Console capture no longer leaves a disposed global writer after parallel tests (#4749)** — production console synchronization, worker captures, and scoped redirects now share serialized ownership with test captures, restore the original `Console.Out` / `Console.Error` references before captured writers are disposed, and verify the recovery invariant before releasing ownership.
- **LSP position-file reads remain bounded when files grow concurrently (#4750)** — disk-backed position-line caching now streams through the 4 MiB byte limit, preserves multibyte text across read boundaries, and returns `position_file_too_large` before over-limit bytes are decoded.
- **Suggestion persistence preserves structured test and recipe identifiers (#4751)** — high-entropy redaction now recognizes multi-word PascalCase, snake_case, leading-underscore, embedded-numeric, and slash/hyphen identifiers while continuing to redact opaque mixed-character secrets and known structured credential formats.
- **Hotspot-sorted symbols no longer repeat physical definitions (#4753)** — audit ranking now combines case-insensitive reference-name variants before ordering and limiting, so each `symbol_id` appears once and offset-based pages remain deterministic without overlap.
- **`map --exclude-tests` now matches the `files` production-source scope (#4754)** — without an explicit `--path`, both commands apply the same production-source preset; explicit path scopes also keep matching cross-command file counts.
- **`recipes --query` now accepts separated values (#4755)** — recipe listing now recognizes both `--query <filter>` and `--query=<filter>` through the canonical CLI flag schema, including option-shaped filter values while preserving a precise missing-value diagnostic.
- **Audit recipe row selection now matches regular search behavior (#4759)** — Row-producing recipe output applies `--first-per-file` and deterministic `--sample` before result limits, sizes sample candidate windows from the requested sample, preserves selectors in generated replay commands, reports selection metadata without exposing or accepting unsafe raw continuation cursors, and rejects selectors for recipe shapes that cannot represent them.
- **Console-sensitive tests no longer capture concurrent request-id logs (#4798)** — every test class that owns process-global console streams now belongs to a non-parallel collection, preventing MCP request-id and global diagnostic lines from unrelated tests from entering captured stdout or stderr.
- **Console capture restoration assertions no longer race parallel tests (#4800, #4808)** — the timeout regression test now snapshots and verifies `Console.Out` and `Console.Error` while holding the shared console ownership gate, preventing another test from replacing a writer during the assertion.
- **Installer cancellation coverage now waits for a complete PID under load (#4801)** — the hung-installer test uses a bounded readiness waiter and starts cancellation only after the PID file contains a positive integer, avoiding empty-file parse failures during parallel test runs.
- **MCP timeout-lease coverage no longer null-dereferences under full-suite load (#4807)** — the regression test now uses an ID-specific readiness signal, scheduler headroom, a bounded blocked-state observation, and typed JSON response assertions so concurrency regressions produce actionable test failures.
- **Isolated global-tool-log home-shorthand tests from sandbox writability fallback (#4810)** — the test now verifies the resolver's normalized first candidate through a no-write-probe test seam, while production resolution continues to require a writable directory.

#### Internal

- **Ubuntu net8 coverage now runs in complementary shards** — `IndexCommandRunnerTests` and the remaining suite run in parallel with coverage enabled in both shards, while full restore, audit, lint, publish, and artifact work stays on one primary shard to shorten the Build and Test critical path without duplicating primary validation.
- **Removed four disconnected private helpers reported by actionable unused analysis (#4739)** — deleted obsolete plugin language-extension aggregation, graph filtering, impact-kind, and full-scan checkpoint-save code while retaining two members that are used across partial-class files.
- **Index-watch readiness tests no longer starve under full-suite load (#4752)** — the top-level watch cancellation fixtures now use dedicated workers and asynchronous readiness signals, distinguish startup exits from observation timeouts, and drain watch tasks before temporary-project cleanup.
- **Made LSP server-busy cancellation coverage deterministic (#4785)** — the backpressure test now holds the active symbol request at an explicit synchronization boundary and stages the cancellation frame until both the request and blocked response write are observed, removing its fixed-delay race under full-suite load.
- **Made the dense C# switch-expression runaway guard resilient to full-suite load (#4792)** — the 10,000-arm correctness fixture now uses a broad 15-second regression tripwire instead of an 8-second benchmark-like threshold, preventing ordinary host contention from causing flaky Release/net8.0 suite failures while still catching quadratic extraction regressions.

### [1.39.4] - 2026-07-23

#### Changed

- **Interrupted bulk FTS setup and cleanup can recover without a process restart** — If trigger suspension fails after the owner marker is written, including after a partial trigger drop, or if restoration or rebuild fails while a bulk guard is unwinding, the writer now best-effort downgrades the marker to owner-independent recovery state and rethrows the original error. A later request in the same process can restore triggers, rebuild searchable FTS state, and clear the marker.
- **Large incremental indexes now avoid recurring full-index FTS optimize** — Full-scan and MCP indexing switch to trigger-free bulk FTS rebuild/optimize only when at least three-fifths of the indexed byte set is dirty. Rewritten files use the larger of their persisted and current sizes, and the total restores shrink excess while also accounting for planned stale deletions, so large rewrites, deletes, and renames choose the policy from a consistent pre-update footprint. The purge runs inside the selected FTS guard. Planned stale IDs are excluded from C# static-interface and reusable-stat snapshots, preventing both obsolete implicit references and a plan-to-scan reappearing file from being skipped after its old row is purged. Snapshot path filtering is allocated only when non-purged indexed rows unused by the current targets outnumber those targets. MCP also invalidates C# contract reuse when a purge removes static-interface contracts, so a clean retry repairs implementers left unprocessed by a partial scan. Smaller updates and scoped CLI updates replace the recurring full optimize with an incremental segment merge whose minimum work target is 1,000 pages. SQLite processes complete segments, so the actual page count may exceed that target. A dedicated merge cadence leaves the since-optimize counter intact for `optimize --dry-run` recommendations, while transactional purge cancellation and bulk-guard abandonment preserve FTS consistency. Fresh and explicit rebuild behavior remains unchanged, and scoped JSON adds `fts_merge_ran` without removing the legacy optimize signal.
- **Large reference files no longer create a nested SAVEPOINT for every 71 references during production indexing** — Full scan, scoped update, MCP indexing, and TypeScript augmentation rebuild now explicitly delegate reference-batch atomicity to their existing file transaction. Public writer APIs retain their #1518 per-batch rollback contract, while guarded internal paths roll back all reference and context rows with the caller's file transaction. A controlled repository-scale model fixes the reduction from 5,009 reference-batch scopes to zero across 321,352 references in 856 files.
- **Large-repository maintenance lookups now stay index-bound** — Index initialization adds checksum and per-file issue lookup indexes, while extension-changing rename cleanup replaces its parameterized `LIKE` scan with an indexed ordinal range without changing literal wildcard, extensionless, or exact-stem behavior.
- **C# static-interface lookup construction now parses generic declarations only for contract-owning interfaces** — the shared full-scan, scoped-update, and MCP workspace lookup first discovers contract containers, returns immediately when none exist, and then scans only matching interface declarations. A 20,000-interface fixture reduces measured lookup allocation from 6,529,440 bytes to 872 bytes while preserving partial declarations, duplicate names, generic substitution, and contract order.
- **C# static-interface preflights now avoid repository-wide work while preserving incremental references** — scoped updates trust authoritative negative source evidence, use bounded path-first transition probes, group common checksum/stem cleanup keys, and reuse stat-matched persisted checksums instead of rescanning the full index or reopening every unchanged target. Git-derived update paths are planned directly from persisted C# rows, so commit/range updates do not stream every live target again merely to compute cleanup checksums; NUL-delimited Git name-status parsing preserves non-ASCII, tab, and newline paths without quoted-path ambiguity. Incomplete-workspace deferral resolves all candidate paths to persisted C# rows in cache-neutral batches of at most 500 instead of issuing one SQLite query per non-C# target. Persisted workspace reads now probe member-capable `symbols(file_id, kind)` rows first and fetch interface declarations only for exact retained container names, so negative and LIKE-decoy-only runs never materialize every plain interface. Full CLI and MCP scans skip source, persisted-symbol, and lookup materialization for an unchanged authoritative true or false workspace only when the prior index is explicitly complete and GraphReady and all filter/version/root/hotspot/stat/language-transition checks still match; legacy or partial metadata falls back safely. Full scans neither create nor consume HEAD-only directory checkpoints and delete legacy checkpoint files after their first immutable input barrier. Each scanned directory contributes one pre-listing baseline, while content/identity-bound ignore, language-map, pattern, submodule, and nested-repository inputs share the same bounded snapshot; pattern enumeration and safety failures make it incomplete instead of silently dropping rules. Full, expanded-update, and MCP consumers validate that snapshot immediately before domain/index-state mutation and again before readiness without retaining the former after-traversal stat map. First-barrier instability preserves prior rows, trust, evidence, purge, and FTS recovery state; C# file drift found while still read-only can promote one complete raw prepass and all-C# refresh, while later drift, fatal discovery gaps, reappeared cleanup paths, and binary/oversized skip-record races roll back or defer mutations and leave evidence unknown for a clean retry. Interrupted-FTS and rebuild repairs run after the first barrier when a scan snapshot is present, and otherwise at the mode-specific mutation boundary. Partial MCP scans derive an authoritative retained/purge plan from successfully listed subtrees and conservatively transition absent persisted C# rows only where discovery was complete. Cleanup candidate SQL stays C#-scoped and cache-neutral in batches of at most 500. Indexed ASCII `NOCASE` and managed case folding only prefilter alias candidates; deletion requires a non-exact spelling and a matching filesystem file identity inside the same case-fold bucket, preserving distinct Unicode pairs, mixed-policy paths, and cross-target hardlinks. Raw built-in source evidence is observed before hooks, filters, and row caps, and managed keyword-boundary validation rejects LIKE-only decoys.
- **C# static-interface workspace prepasses now read persisted contract rows once** — full scans, scoped updates, and MCP indexing derive both the reusable-symbol snapshot and the pending-path contract-presence bit from one prepared SQLite reader. Existing public presence queries remain available, while the indexing hot path avoids a second workspace-wide contract scan and preserves removed or changed pending-contract behavior.
- **C# metadata-target propagation now scales linearly through deep inheritance chains** — indexing builds reverse dependency edges once and visits each newly resolved target through a work queue, avoiding repeated repository-wide class scans on reverse-ordered codebases. Stable reruns also skip unchanged metadata-target row writes while cancellation remains wired through CLI and MCP finalization.
- **C# static-interface prepasses now use one bounded file snapshot per stable candidate** — full scans, scoped updates, and MCP indexing authorize and open each stable candidate once, reuse that handle for raw probing and positive-candidate decoding, and scan comments and strings without allocating a second whole-content mask. A candidate mutated during the read is discarded and reauthorized/reopened once, including atomic-save replacements. Large C# workspaces with many static-interface probe candidates therefore avoid duplicate file opens and multi-megabyte transient allocations while preserving encoding, size, mutation, cancellation, and authorization safeguards.
- **Large C# workspaces now build static-interface contract lookups once per indexing snapshot** — full scan, scoped update, and MCP indexing reuse the immutable lookup produced by the C# prepass instead of rescanning every workspace symbol for every C# file. Direct reference-extractor calls retain their existing per-call behavior.
- **Large indexing batches now refresh hotspot reference aggregates once instead of once per file** — Full scan, scoped update, MCP indexing, and TypeScript augmentation rebuild collect dirty file IDs behind transaction/savepoint checkpoints, discard failed-file work, and run one set-based aggregate refresh at finalization. Readiness is still rechecked and cleared inside every mutation transaction; refresh and conditional trust restoration share one transaction, so cancellation remains safely degraded and a previously unready database is never promoted.
- **Reference-graph refresh no longer rewrites already-current identity rows** — Source-symbol identity, target-resolution state, and self-reference maintenance now use NULL-safe changed-value predicates across every indexed language. Stable graph rebuilds still recompute candidates and preserve the existing transaction, cancellation, readiness, and final `changes()` contracts, but avoid three table-wide rounds of index-maintaining no-op writes. Trigger-backed regression coverage fixes zero physical identity writes on a stable rerun, one repair per corrupted phase, and rollback across refresh phases.
- **Incremental reference-graph finalization now follows only committed dirty identities** — full-scan, scoped-update, and MCP indexing retain old/new symbol names and reciprocal edges across deletion, rename, and language transitions, then rebuild candidates only for affected references. Every scoped update and candidate phase is driven by dirty reference primary-key seeks, C# instantiate grouping starts from dirty lookup names, and tiny production scopes skip the whole-table reference count. Transaction rollbacks do not leak dirty state, cancellation leaves the readiness contract degraded for a safe retry, and fresh/rebuild, missing-contract, or broad changes still use the full refresh. On a controlled 324,000-reference repository snapshot, a one-reference refresh fell from a 1,567.433 ms median to 90.547 ms (17.31× faster) while matching a subsequent full refresh.
- **Large-repository unchanged-file snapshots now materialize in one pass** — CLI and MCP indexing pre-size the reusable-stat dictionary from counts already available after discovery, reject malformed SQLite stat types in the snapshot query, and avoid both a temporary candidate list and duplicate path values.
- **Large atomic-file reference writes materialize context rows in wider windows** — full-scan, scoped-update, and MCP indexing now group complete 71-reference batches for reference-line insertion and lookup, bounded by SQLite's 333-row parameter limit and 32 batches, while preserving reference INSERT, progress, cancellation, and rollback boundaries. A controlled 321K-reference persistence benchmark reduced elapsed time by about 12% and current-thread allocations by about 9%.
- **Large reference sets now avoid redundant post-processing allocations** — C# files without applicable using-alias rewrites skip alias dedupe entirely, rewritten aliases compact duplicates in one stable pass, BCL Regex auditing reuses container identity values directly, and repeated caller/callee names share cycle normalization results across all languages.
- **Large reference graphs now resolve through bounded composite lookups** — Fresh databases and read migrations add file/name and folded-name/container indexes for source and ranked-candidate resolution across all languages, plus a partial covering index for reverse resolved-edge probes used by mutual-recursion refresh.
- **Large-tree scans now enumerate each normally visited directory once** — The default per-directory case-sensitivity probe and the main entry walk share one ordered, scan-local snapshot while preserving custom probes, legacy test enumeration, dangling-entry diagnostics, and single-error enumeration-failure diagnostics.
- **CI failure telemetry skips redundant project evaluation** — Retry filtering and TRX summaries now launch the already-built telemetry assembly directly instead of invoking `dotnet run`.
- **Pre-test CI failures skip empty artifact actions** — Test-result, dump, and coverage uploads now require the test step to have started, avoiding no-op upload setup after restore or build failures.
- **Temporary-project cleanup avoids an eager filesystem walk** — Clean fixtures now attempt recursive deletion directly, while attribute normalization and bounded Windows recovery remain available after a real deletion failure.
- **SQLite fixture cleanup releases pools only when required** — Seeded-file writes and clean database deletion no longer trigger unconditional process-wide pool clearing; Windows retries still release pools when a file is actually locked, while raw-database archive fixtures opt into per-connection pool invalidation before direct file reads.
- **Hook scheduling coverage uses a compact assembly** — Full-scan scheduling tests now stage the dedicated hook-isolation fixture instead of copying the much larger test assembly into a worker directory.
- **Unix shell tests skip before Windows fixture setup** — Installer and container-entrypoint cases now skip during discovery on Windows instead of constructing temporary directories and returning from the test body.
- **Production query boundaries reuse indexed workspaces** — Related C# order-by comma and range-scope, ternary-operator, throw-expression, query-terminal, postfix, casted local-select, and nullable-suffix cases now share one production CLI indexing subprocess per syntax family while retaining distinct assertions.
- **Seeded query boundaries reuse databases** — C# generic type-pattern, query range-scope, foreach-shadowing, lambda-parameter, and declaration-pattern variants now share graph-ready databases by family while path filters preserve their exact result contracts.
- **Production SQL boundaries reuse indexed workspaces** — Line-end comment, `USING` / `MERGE`, semicolonless temporary-table, non-code masking, and TRUNCATE variants now share one production CLI indexing subprocess per family while path filters preserve exact contracts.
- **Non-coverage net8 lanes run complementary test shards** — Windows and macOS split `IndexCommandRunnerTests` from the remainder into separate processes; Ubuntu coverage remains full-suite, retries retain or intersect shard filters, and artifacts include shard identity.
- **Dense extractor guards retain CI timing headroom** — C# and Java dense-constructor fixtures remain half-sized while restoring ten-second runaway ceilings, keeping the shorter workloads without false failures from coverage instrumentation.
- **MCP C# stat-race coverage is enumeration-order independent** — Source drift is injected after final workspace validation and before the file loop, so the actual-skip revalidation contract no longer depends on native directory order.
- **Incremental TypeScript augmentation refreshes are scoped to changed interface names** — full scans, `--files` updates, and MCP indexing now track old and new interface names, including stale-file deletion and persisted TypeScript-to-other-language transitions, then delete and rebuild only augmentation rows sharing those names in bounded batches while preserving file module classification. Fresh/rebuild runs, broad dirty sets, contract or project-root changes, and upfront forced extractor refreshes retain the authoritative full fallback; runtime JavaScript/TypeScript configuration refreshes track every refreshed file and use that same adaptive fallback. In a controlled 50,002-declaration augmentation rebuild with one dirty merged name, median elapsed time fell by about 44% and current-thread allocation by more than 99%.
- **Large TypeScript interface sets use allocation-bounded augmentation grouping** — augmentation rebuilds now index declarations in one pass, materialize declaration-index lists only for genuinely merged interfaces, and classify each module file once. A controlled 50,002-declaration benchmark reduced current-thread allocations by about 18% while preserving first-seen group and declaration order.

#### Fixed

- **Index mutation recovery now preserves committed and reappearing state across failure boundaries** — Bulk FTS guards observe durable writer commits before throwable post-commit bookkeeping and WAL checkpoints, so MCP cleanup rebuilds searchable state before clearing its recovery marker even when the caller mutation flag was not yet set. Transaction finalization keeps the writer gate until post-commit actions have completed or failed, and rollback detaches its completed transaction before exposing a terminal state to concurrent disposal. The primary process marker remains legacy-readable `pid:<pid>`, while a separately associated PID-bound start-time generation or per-process token detects current-PID reuse; persistent cleanup triggers prevent an older writer from leaving that generation stale, and unverifiable ownership remains conservatively active. File purges now honor cancellation while waiting for the transaction gate, and expanded C# cleanup guards compare normalized repository `IndexPath` values so an exact reappearing row is preserved until a clean retry. CLI and MCP index responses now retain discovered C# and SQL presence across pre-write aborts and per-file failures, including fresh, rebuild, and partial discovery, so readiness no longer depends on which file was persisted first. MCP also demotes the durable SQL graph contract before mutation and only restamps it after clean completion, keeping both the immediate response and subsequent readers degraded after a partial run. C# prepass reads now close their snapshot handle before restating the path and treat same-timestamp length changes as mutations, while Git subprocess output is decoded as UTF-8 on every platform so canonical non-ASCII commit paths remain intact on Windows.
- **Published trimmed builds now index JSON keys without reflection (#4709)** — JSON and dependency-lock extraction now encode property names without reflection-based serialization, so files containing keys such as `$schema` or `node_modules/...` no longer leave rebuilt indexes partial.

#### Internal

- **Project-marker fingerprints now share one cross-language tree traversal** — full/update CLI and MCP indexing compute C#, VB, F#, and MSBuild marker fingerprints in one bounded directory-tree walk. Distinct marker globs retain their platform matching behavior, while per-language budgets, truncation warnings, ignore and repository boundaries, and authorization failures keep their prior contracts.

### [1.39.3] - 2026-07-21

#### Fixed

- **Windows release validation no longer flakes on SQLite WAL cleanup or pattern timeout snapshot churn** — the release tests now keep the external WAL writer alive through artifact comparison and reuse one published pattern extractor snapshot, preventing spurious missing sidecars and duplicate timeout diagnostics.

### [1.39.2] - 2026-07-21

#### Fixed

- **Per-file indexing failures now retain actionable diagnostics** — full-scan and update failures record the active phase and a bounded safe detail, exceptions retain their extraction stack across the parallel full-scan boundary, isolated symbol-worker failures report a redacted origin frame, and long stack frames preserve their source-line suffix instead of losing it behind a truncated method signature.

### [1.39.1] - 2026-07-21

#### Fixed

- **Release install verification now authenticates GitHub attestation checks** — the published-release smoke job supplies its read-only automatic GitHub token to the installer, so the default strict provenance policy can verify release assets instead of failing because GitHub CLI is unauthenticated.

### [1.39.0] - 2026-07-21

#### Added

- **MCP `resources/read` now supports bounded ranges and continuation (#4544)** — callers can select inclusive line ranges and a UTF-8 byte budget, while bounded defaults, explicit truncation metadata, and version-bound cursors keep large single-line and multi-line resources from being fully materialized before pagination. Pages are also limited to 1,000 logical lines, adapt to tighter enclosing MCP/HTTP response limits, share the aggregate frame ceiling across JSON-RPC batch items (preserving IDs with compact structured errors when an item cannot fit), and use one SQLite read snapshot. Read-only or immutable legacy databases without the new partial indexes use a metadata-only, VM-step-budgeted `idx_chunks_file` fallback; budget exhaustion and incomplete or unsafe indexed storage return structured errors instead of partial success or unbounded scans.
- **Definition discovery can group partial types into logical families (#4566)** — `definition`, `symbols`, and symbol-mode `inspect` now accept `--group-partials`, use the same qualified self-identity as `impact`, preserve unrelated and nested non-partial declarations, keep audit sorts stable, distinguish limited output from query-wide totals, and expose authoritative logical and physical counts without materializing every impact definition.
- **Added conventional `help <command>` routing (#4575)** — `cdidx help <command> [subcommand]` now renders the existing command help without dispatching the target. Public commands and supported command or nested aliases, including `db --integrity-check`, are accepted; internal usage keys are rejected, and missing or unknown targets return usage exit `1` with stable error codes and nearest command/subcommand suggestions.
- Added `cdidx optimize --dry-run` as a read-only FTS5 maintenance preview with database, core-table, FTS, freelist, readiness, lock, recommendation, duration-estimate, and planned-operation diagnostics.
- **High-volume query outputs now share bounded projections and stable pagination (#4585)** — `definition`, `find`, `status`, `hotspots`, `references`, `callers`, `callees`, `impact`, and `map` accept shared field projection and opaque response cursors, report returned/total/omitted counts, and can enforce a whole-response JSON byte budget. Compact location responses keep their established top-level keys and lightweight rows while gaining the shared metadata; compact and aliased commands plus read-only batch children use the same hard cap. Nested graph and map section collections page as rows with collection-specific totals, late pages push offsets into the query layer, scalar map projections skip unused ranked sections, and explicit definition bodies remain available through `body`, `body_content`, and `all` projections while excluded bodies are not materialized.
- **Adversarial edge cases retain their response contracts (#4585)** — impact definition cursors page only definitions without changing caller/fallback mode; plain compact maps preserve their section arrays; conflicting map shape controls fail explicitly; compact explicit body fields override compact defaults; diagnostics become metadata control records; and parser/capture errors never escape the requested hard byte cap.
- **Added symmetric `find --context` windows (#4621)** — `find --context <n>` now sets both snippet sides, while explicit `--before` and `--after` independently override their corresponding sides regardless of option order. Values share the existing 1,000-line context bound, option-shaped literal queries remain literal, and shared help, shell completions, direct parsing, and JSON-lines batch dispatch expose the same contract.

#### Changed

- **Large-index diagnostics now identify expensive phases** — `index --json --memory-trace` reports C# prepass, extraction, reference-graph, text-index, finalization, and full-scan commit boundaries, while partial updates report the corresponding shared phases.
- **Automatic full-scan parallelism avoids high-core contention** — the default worker count now follows the CPU count up to eight instead of sixteen, while `--parallelism` and `CDIDX_INDEX_PARALLELISM` still accept explicit values through sixteen.
- **Reference resolution consolidates repeated graph lookups** — candidate counts, unique target families, target IDs, and stable keys are now derived by one aggregate per reference instead of repeated correlated subqueries across every supported language.
- **Unique symbol families are shared across graph fallbacks** — non-C#, C#, and C# attribute resolution now reuse one connection-local language/name aggregation instead of grouping the complete symbol table three times per graph refresh.
- **Source files cross the symbol-worker boundary once** — requests are serialized directly to UTF-8 bytes instead of materializing a UTF-16 JSON string and encoding it again for every file, with Unicode coverage across C#, Java, TypeScript, Python, Go, and Rust.
- **Symbol-worker responses stream as UTF-8** — extracted symbol batches are serialized directly to the worker stdout stream, removing the matching UTF-16 JSON allocation and re-encoding pass on the return path.
- **Worker responses stay as bytes in the parent** — a bounded, buffered UTF-8 frame reader now feeds response bytes directly to JSON deserialization while preserving frame limits, CRLF handling, cancellation, and persistent-worker remainder buffering.
- **Graph-neutral updates skip repository-wide recursion work** — incremental full scans, scoped updates, and MCP indexing now distinguish cleanup that actually changes symbol/reference identity rows, so text-only source edits avoid a whole-graph pass while symbol and reference mutations still refresh once per batch.
- **Small incremental runs batch FTS segment maintenance** — full scans, scoped updates, and MCP indexing now share the 25-run incremental optimize threshold, while fresh indexes and rebuilds continue to rebuild and optimize FTS5 immediately.
- **Index completion avoids repeated whole-reader readiness work** — full scans, scoped updates, and MCP indexing read reference-cap metadata through the active writer transaction without promoting degraded issue state, while hotspot-family validation groups only indexed languages in one symbol pass instead of running a correlated scan for every supported language.
- **`files` positional globs now use path-filter semantics (#4565)** — quoted positional values containing an unescaped `*` or `?`, including recursive patterns such as `**/*.cs`, now behave like `--path <glob>` instead of returning a misleading filename-query miss.
- **Batch is now a complete structured read-only query transport (#4582)** — the schema-owned side-effect-free allowlist now includes `goto` and `audit`; `--json-summary` embeds successful JSON as `result` and stable NDJSON as `results`, retains raw text for text or failed output, and bounds the full serialized stream plus input-line count.
- **Suggestion IDs now remain stable across draft edits (#4588)** — new records use content-independent immutable public IDs, all editable fields participate in a separate `revision_hash`, legacy `hash` values migrate without breaking old references, stale updates/deletes and in-flight submission results cannot overwrite or remove a newer revision, and CLI, export, and MCP output expose both identities.
- **`languages` now separates extension and filename capabilities (#4617)** — CLI/MCP rows publish suffix-only `extensions`, literal `exact_filenames`, `<suffix>` filename-prefix patterns, and per-pattern provenance; language-map suffix overrides reassign affected exact filenames in the catalog just as they do during runtime detection. `legacy_patterns` retains the former combined list during a deprecation window, and round-trip tests verify every advertised typed pattern against actual detection.

#### Fixed

- Codex can now initialize the cdidx MCP server and enumerate its tools. The server negotiates the `2025-06-18` protocol version used by current Codex clients while retaining the older `2025-03-26` and `2024-11-05` versions. The setup guide now uses the shared `config.toml` / `codex mcp add` configuration and explains that a new Codex session is required after registration.
- **JavaScript/TypeScript discriminant guards can now be indexed without a database argument error** — `type_tag` is registered as a persisted reference kind, remains queryable through `references`, and is excluded from runtime caller/callee graphs.
- **Configured MCP request concurrency is now effective and bounded for stdio and HTTP (#4536)** — independent requests execute up to the server limit, including base transports at `maxConcurrency: 1` without double-acquiring the execution gate; the accepted backlog rejects overflow with retry-safe `server_busy`, queued request ids remain cancellable, timeouts retain their lease until live actions drain, session mutations preserve receive order, and request-scoped HTTP writers keep every response attached to its originating POST.
- **Top-level JSON-RPC Invalid Request responses now include `id: null` (#4538)** — Scalar, `null`, and malformed-object frames now use the same standards-compliant response shape as invalid batch elements, while valid notifications remain response-free.
- **`resources/list` now uses generation-aware keyset cursors (#4541)** — Opaque, bounded cursors resume from a stable file anchor, file mutations return an explicit restart-required stale-index error, and mutable read-only legacy databases require migration instead of silently treating missing generation tracking as generation zero. Canonical, unambiguous immutable legacy snapshots remain safely pageable.
- **`resources/list` responses are now byte-bounded and omission-aware (#4542)** — Pages measure the complete JSON-RPC envelope against an optional `maxBytes` budget and the active HTTP response cap, continue with an opaque cursor before crossing the effective limit, and report bounded counts and reasons for every omitted resource. HTTP JSON-RPC batches also budget the complete response array, including brackets and commas, so multiple large resource pages share the transport cap while preserving every response ID.
- **MCP transport teardown is now bounded across every exit path (#4543)** — EOF, malformed input, shutdown, and external cancellation share the bounded drain; the initiating HTTP shutdown notification completes its `204`, callbacks that start after the first drain snapshot are still bounded, inline control-write cancellation cannot bypass cleanup, and stdio output disposal waits for accepted late writers. Final diagnostics identify unfinished requests, writes, or callbacks.
- **JSON-RPC batch items now execute with bounded concurrency and durable cancellation (#4545)** — independent items share the global MCP request limit, queued targets remain cancellable without depending on tombstone capacity or TTL, and pre-dispatch returns release their registrations for safe ID reuse. HTTP authenticates before cancellation handling, extracts cross-frame controls before queue admission, and keeps same-batch controls with their queued target; session mutations and repeated IDs retain input-order semantics, per-item failures stay isolated, and response arrays remain in input order.
- **Bounded HTTP MCP request lifetimes and propagated disconnect cancellation (#4546)** — Configurable body-idle and total deadlines now cover request reading, queueing, tool/SQLite execution, and response completion. Established-session response-bearing JSON-RPC requests use serialized, bounded chunked-whitespace probes to detect clients that disconnect after upload, while the initial headerless `initialize` and notifications skip probing so session headers and `204 No Content` semantics are preserved. Probe failure, timeout, disconnect, and shutdown paths cancel active work; cancellation-ignoring work keeps its bounded concurrency and body-budget leases until it actually exits, and output-stream ownership is not handed to a later response while an earlier write is still settling. Non-cooperative response, probe, and SSE output operations share a bounded registry, and probe request-body leases remain held until their underlying output settles.
- **Bounded aggregate HTTP MCP request-body memory (#4548)** — HTTP request bodies now reserve a configurable process-wide byte budget before known-length reads and throughout unknown-length streaming, queueing, execution, and response completion. If canceled MCP work does not stop cooperatively, its reservation remains charged until that work actually completes. Saturation returns a classified HTTP 429, invalid per-request/budget combinations fail startup, health reports effective and live usage, and every terminal failure or shutdown path releases its reservation exactly once.
- **Validated HTTP MCP resource limits and isolated SSE admission (#4550)** — Every present HTTP limit environment variable must now be a positive integer in its documented range or startup fails with the exact variable and accepted range. Long-lived `/events` connections use a separate bounded admission gate, so stream saturation cannot consume POST handler capacity, and `/healthz` reports both effective capacities.
- **MCP metrics writes are now non-blocking and recoverable (#4552)** — metrics events enter a bounded background queue, flush in batches, account for dropped events, and retry later batches with capped exponential backoff. MCP status and ping diagnostics expose queue, failure, and recovery health, while the first runtime failure emits one bounded warning.
- **Incomplete MCP audit shutdowns are now observable and optionally enforceable (#4553)** — audit diagnostics track lifetime queued and written records plus a distinct shutdown-deadline abandoned snapshot, and a bounded path-free warning is emitted when the drain deadline expires. `--audit-log-strict` promotes an otherwise-successful MCP session to runtime exit code 10 after an incomplete flush while preserving an existing nonzero exit.
- **Made the process-wide SQLite schema cache immutable and lifecycle-bounded (#4554)** — column and index lookups now publish frozen snapshots that callers cannot corrupt, while per-path shared state remains available to active database contexts and is released when the final owner is disposed.
- **SQLite `CANTOPEN` validation failures now report their actual cause (#4556)** — File and directory preflight, extended SQLite codes, and bounded OS probes distinguish missing databases, permission/traversal denials, WAL/SHM sidecar failures, invalid URIs, and unknown open failures while keeping provider messages and sensitive paths out of diagnostics.
- **Query-only SQLite operations no longer mutate index state (#4557)** — Database callers now declare query, indexing, migration, or repair intent. Query-only CLI, LSP, export, dry-run, and MCP paths skip persistent pragmas and opportunistic migrations, preserve database and sidecar artifacts through generation-validated private WAL snapshots, refresh long-lived readers when the source changes, and only report interrupted batches. Cross-database dependency targets use the same snapshot lease and release it after the attaching connection closes; persistent snapshot-copy I/O failures now report temporary-storage remediation instead of WAL churn. Readiness demotion runs solely from the explicit rebuild repair path.
- **WAL truncate checkpoints now preserve SQLite result diagnostics (#4558)** — Both instance and read-only-fallback checkpoint paths read `(busy, log, checkpointed)`, report busy or remaining pages as unsuccessful with bounded machine reasons and counts, and expose the structured result through query and status diagnostics without leaking raw exception text.
- **Database permission hardening failures are now portable and auditable (#4559)** — Unix mode operations default to a warning-producing `best_effort` policy so SQLite-capable FUSE and network mounts remain usable, while `CDIDX_DB_PERMISSION_POLICY=strict` requires enforcement. Status JSON exposes the effective policy and support-safe machine-readable diagnostics.
- **SQLite migrations now track transaction and foreign-key ownership explicitly (#4560)** — opportunistic read migrations detect caller-owned transactions before opening their own transaction, unrelated `BEGIN` errors propagate without partial DDL, and table rebuilds verify foreign keys are disabled before `BEGIN` and restore the original effective mode after success or rollback.
- **Bounded NDJSON streams now end explicitly and report partial results (#4561)** — Plain and recipe/audit `search` reserves byte budget for a terminal record with authoritative or lower-bound counts, selection/interruption reasons, limits, omissions, and recovery guidance; `symbols` and `files` keep their raw discovery stream shape, including an empty stream for zero results. Byte-capped partial output exits with code 11 unless callers explicitly pass `--allow-partial`; unbudgeted diagnostics and envelope serialization are rejected. JSON envelopes preserve any stream terminal in dedicated metadata instead of counting it as a result row.
- **Conflicting or ineffective output-format options now fail explicitly (#4562)** — `--json` no longer silently loses to CSV, TSV, quickfix, or command-owned JSON schemas, `--pretty` with explicit or implicit NDJSON now points callers to `--json=array --pretty`, while single-document recipe, aggregation, summary, count, and compact JSON outputs remain pretty-printable. Dash-prefixed `--query` values remain literals, and invalid modes, unsupported flags, and command-unsupported formats keep their primary diagnostics instead of being masked by a secondary combination error.
- **Discovery JSON now keeps its selected schema and reports generated-file filtering (#4563)** — `symbols` and `files` preserve raw NDJSON or array output across zero and byte-capped results, including trust diagnostics on diagnostic-only zero-result arrays and exact byte boundaries. DB-backed discovery query contexts, file counts, and every repository-map JSON format expose schema-aware generated-code policy/availability and excluded generated-file counts, while legacy schemas report a requested filter and count as unavailable instead of claiming exclusion occurred.
- **JSON query failures now use one versioned error envelope (#4564)** — validation failures for `search`, `find`, and `status`, missing `goto` definitions, and missing or out-of-range `excerpt` coordinates now preserve their documented non-success exit codes while returning parseable JSON with stable `status` and `error_code` fields.
- **Recovery hints now provide safe structured argv (#4567)** — excerpt and body recovery payloads preserve the current apphost or `dotnet` plus assembly prefix in a primary `argv` array, while the legacy display-only command is escaped for its declared POSIX sh or PowerShell context.
- **Canonicalized default caller and callee edge kinds (#4568)** — default graph rows now use the shared `call`, `instantiate`, and `subscribe` vocabulary across labels, kind lists, filters, and count keys; type and metadata edges remain available through references or explicit kind filters, and C# tuple-return declarations no longer emit a phantom call to `static`.
- **Graph edges now resolve to persisted symbol identities (#4569)** — Reference rows retain resolved target IDs or overload-family keys plus explicit ambiguous/unresolved candidates behind a versioned readiness marker, so C# dependency and qualified caller/impact traversal, recursion flags, and reference JSON no longer connect unrelated same-named symbols across containers or languages; no-op and deletion-only indexing also repair legacy identity data.
- **Ambiguous inspect targets now stay in separate candidate bundles (#4570)** — `inspect` and MCP `analyze_symbol` label each definition with stable ID/qualified-name/signature/path selectors and scope references, callers, and callees to that identity instead of merging same-named implementations.
- **Unified CLI help and completion metadata (#4571)** — command help for shared-parser commands now derives accepted flags and descriptions from the schema used by parser validation and shell completions, while dedicated and nested parsers retain their exact usage syntax instead of showing partial parent-command options. Optional-subcommand completion keeps parent flags available for `recipes` and `suggestions`, nested workspace completion includes clear/deactivate, dependency recovery hints reuse canonical flag spellings, search usage separates query modes, and `status --explain sqlite_connection_policy` documents SQLite/WAL diagnostics.
- **`inspect` now resolves indexed file paths and coordinates strictly (#4572)** — an exact indexed positional path now selects file inspection before symbol lookup, while explicit missing paths and lines beyond EOF return structured `E019_FILE_NOT_FOUND` or `E020_LINE_OUT_OF_RANGE` failures instead of unrelated nearest symbols.
- **Map scope, depth, candidate counts, and freshness metadata are now consistent (#4573)** — Module depth is aggregated after scope filters, scoped output no longer carries the workspace-wide decomposition plan, Issue-draft counts and truncation use the evaluated candidate set, and map JSON exposes the current index HEAD metadata while labeling the legacy full-scan stamp separately.
- **Invalid CLI arguments now produce one command-specific diagnostic (#4574)** — derived inspect line ranges no longer look like duplicate explicit options, invalid field/check tokens suppress dependent empty-list errors, every `recipes` validation and byte-limit failure retains its own Usage, completion errors render once, and trailing formatting flags stay out of line-mode inspect queries.
- **`status --stale-after` now activates the freshness gate (#4576)** — a valid CLI threshold implies `--check`, always includes the workspace gate even with scoped checks, preserves fresh and stale exit codes, and records the effective threshold plus `explicit` or `implied_by_stale_after` mode in JSON `query_context`.
- **`find --all` now makes partial row and count scans explicit (#4578)** — Streaming JSON rows end with terminal scan metadata, count objects carry the same authority and recovery state, formats that cannot carry row-terminal metadata are rejected, and safety-cap truncation exits with code 11 unless callers explicitly pass `--allow-partial`.
- **Machine-readable utility responses now expose the shared JSON API version (#4579)** — Success and failure payloads for database restore/backup maintenance, diff, update/upgrade checks, hooks, workspace/config, language/version inventory, test-extractor, and index runs now carry `api_version` through the shared `IVersionedJsonResult` contract. `test-extractor` success uses a versioned envelope while preserving its nested symbol properties.
- **Index dry-run is now non-destructive and memory-diagnostic complete (#4580)** — rebuild previews no longer require destructive confirmation, and `--dry-run --memory-trace --json` emits live phase and memory samples without changing workspace or database artifacts.
- **Limited hotspot queries now use bounded maintained SQL aggregates (#4581)** — indexing maintains compact per-file logical-reference totals, and symbol/file/name hotspot ranking selects an index-ordered bounded candidate frontier before ambiguity joins instead of regrouping the complete raw reference graph for every query. Logical-site aliases are deduplicated consistently, cross-file context/identity mutations refresh or demote trust transactionally, and cancellation interrupts in-flight SQLite aggregate work.
- **Validation limits now preserve authoritative totals and SARIF severity (#4583)** — JSON, compact, and SARIF validation output reports returned, total, omitted, and truncation metadata from the full matching set, while informational findings map to SARIF `note` results, retain their actionability metadata, and expose degraded legacy validation data instead of presenting it as authoritative zero findings.
- **Multi named-query searches now honor compact projection (#4584)** — `search` now serializes every named query as lightweight `{file,line}` rows under `--format compact`, while preserving query names, query text, per-query counts, truncation metadata, and the aggregate JSON byte cap.
- **`cdidx report` now includes the failure that recommended running it (#4586)** — unhandled CLI failures save one bounded, redacted event before printing the report guidance, and the next report includes its timestamp, binary details, command and exception categories, exit code, and sanitized diagnostics even when lifecycle logging is disabled, without recording literal arguments.
- **Suggestions now work with explicit databases in shared temporary roots (#4589)** — macOS/Linux shared-directory databases keep their sidecar and lock state in a deterministic owner-only user scope, while path and permission failures return structured `E021_SUGGESTION_STORE_UNAVAILABLE` diagnostics instead of exit 99.
- **Auth-token audits now rank credential context ahead of structural token noise (#4590)** — Each auth-token child query ranks tightly coupled credential identifiers, runtime header use, and secret-provider symbols before applying its result limit, while comments, documentation/help text, regex definitions, and parser, LSP, syntax-token, or `CancellationToken` contexts are down-ranked. Paired true/false fixtures now enforce top-N precision across bearer/authorization, GitHub/API/access-token, and token-secret searches.
- **Watch sub-runs are cancellable without replacing process-global stdout (#4591)** — Ctrl-C, SIGTERM, and embedding-host cancellation now flow through the top-level token into active incremental or full-rescan work, including FTS rebuild/optimization and SQLite planner maintenance, while preserving second-Ctrl-C force exit. Interrupted bulk FTS work restores synchronization triggers and leaves recoverable state for the next run; cancelled long-lived MCP requests also suppress duplicate dispose-time planner maintenance. Index command output is captured through a runner-scoped writer, keeping concurrent and embedded stdout isolated, with deterministic coverage for idle and active cancellation.
- **Scan, status, and watch now share membership and invalidation rules (#4592)** — `.cdidx` sidecars are consistently excluded from indexed source membership, while ignore files and workspace pattern/plugin inputs bypass watch filtering long enough to trigger a debounced full scan. Subproject watches observe ancestor ignore files. Extractor reconciliation refreshes the process registry generation, disables unchanged-file reuse, unloads prior workspace plugins, and reloads current pattern/plugin inputs while preserving explicitly registered host extractors, so persisted rows are regenerated even for same-extension edits. Plugin assemblies are loaded without retaining a Windows file lock, allowing refreshes to remove or replace them. Ignore/unignore plus pattern edits, deletion, and plugin removal coverage keep reconciliation behavior aligned across all three paths.
- **Pattern configuration loading is now transactional and repairable (#4593)** — sidecars are fully parsed, regex-compiled, and checked against the symbol-kind catalog before paths, rules, and budget are committed. Invalid content no longer leaks rule budget or remains permanently loaded, repaired or transiently unreadable files can be retried without restarting the process, and accepted sidecars are not reopened by later extension probes.
- **Watch now reconciles the initial-scan handoff before reporting ready (#4594)** — the filesystem watcher subscribes before a startup reconciliation scan, drains the buffered startup generation, and emits `watching` only after every startup sub-run succeeds. A failed startup generation exits non-zero instead of discarding the edit and declaring a stale watcher ready.
- **Pattern rule budgets and timeout cooldowns are now workspace-scoped (#4595)** — immutable snapshots give each workspace its own 128-rule budget and bounded timeout state; trusted user patterns consume budget before lower-precedence workspace patterns, and reindexing releases the replaced snapshot without changing another workspace.
- **Pattern configuration discovery now honors workspace and filesystem boundaries (#4597)** — discovery stops at the explicit workspace root, propagates in-workspace nested sidecars to the bounded symbol worker, follows the active filesystem's case-sensitivity for path identity, and reports sanitized workspace/user provenance in extractor status.
- **Filesystem case probing and filename language detection now share the actual path-case policy (#4601)** — case probes use a private child entry below the target root without mutating ancestor components, including numeric basenames, while exact filenames and filename-prefix patterns follow `path_case_sensitive`; `languages` JSON and MCP output expose this policy.
- **Extractor registrations are now immutable and workspace-scoped (#4602)** — same-language plugins and patterns resolve from workspace snapshots with exposed built-in/user/workspace precedence; explicit-language graph gates, analysis, unused-symbol queries, status, and CLI/MCP language reporting use the indexed workspace snapshot; and generation-checked staged reloads, bounded LRU retention, and post-cancellation retirement prevent reloads, shutdown, or late plugin commits from leaking, resurrecting, or mutating another workspace's active extractors and plugin contexts.
- **Made C-versus-C++ `.h` detection lexical and budget-aware (#4608)** — header scoring now reuses a stateful C/C++ comment and string masker, ignores continued preprocessor payloads, and replaces the first-200-lines cutoff with a 48 KiB UTF-8 scoring budget over full-header or head/middle/tail ranges. Lexical state streams across skipped bytes, translation-phase line splices can form comment and raw-string delimiters, and partial-token sample starts cannot invent line-start markers. Ambiguous decisions expose stable source/confidence metadata through dry-run output, and comment-only or macro-string C++ words no longer promote C headers.
- **A per-file extraction failure no longer hides every successful graph edge or exits as an unconditional success (#4609)** — Full scans and scoped updates commit successful file generations, expose bounded phase-aware file errors, persist completeness separately from freshness, and return partial-result exit code `11` unless `--allow-partial` is explicit. Full-scan JSON also distinguishes extracted from persisted counts. Later scoped updates revalidate the full workspace until the failed file recovers, preventing unrelated updates from clearing the failure and restoring readiness without a rebuild.
- **Valid PostgreSQL table, recursive CTE, and `RETURNS TABLE` files no longer abort SQL extraction (#4610)** — `RETURNS TABLE` result columns now use bounded, quote-aware parenthesis scanning instead of a capture-group range, so supported symbols and references remain indexable when these common PostgreSQL constructs appear separately or together.
- **Authoritative shebangs now resolve ambiguous and unknown extensions (#4611)** — recognized Tcl shebangs override the Perl default for `.t`, recognized shebangs classify unknown extensions such as Python `.txt` scripts, explicit language-map overrides stay authoritative, strong extensions retain precedence, and successful detections record `detection_source: shebang` without trusting malformed, over-limit, or binary/NUL input. The active index database and its sidecars are excluded consistently from CLI/MCP indexing, dry runs, and workspace freshness scans.
- **`.m` and `.pl` now use conservative language classification (#4612)** — authoritative shebangs, bounded strong content markers, and bounded project markers distinguish Objective-C/MATLAB and Perl/Prolog; marker-only scoped updates reclassify dependent files, zero-arity Prolog rules and DCGs are recognized, and an incomplete final code point at the bounded read boundary is decoded safely. Weak or conflicting evidence remains explicit as `ambiguous_m` / `ambiguous_pl`, while shared language registries, query aliases, and new MATLAB and Prolog symbol extractors expose the detected languages without overstating reference or graph support.
